people.imagined: Night in the bamboo grove of Lôi Trúc Lâm. She sits wrapped in a rain-grey cloak among the rite poles, a short pole across her knees, measuring it against her forearm a second time while mist gathers, and listens for whoever is cutting them.
people.subject: The moment: deep night in a bamboo grove, a small old woman sitting on a root among tall rite poles, laying a cut pole along her forearm to measure it a second time. Face: a small, sun-dark, frail face with fine deep lines, a narrow nose, high cheekbones and a mouth pressed in patient stubbornness; dark clear eyes fixed on the shadows between the poles, thin grey brows. Hair: white, drawn into a low knot with one pale green jade pin, a few strands loose in the damp. Body: slight and narrow, bent a little forward at the shoulders, bony wrists, the stillness of someone who has not slept in a bed for weeks. Clothing: soft robes of rain-grey silk in three layers, the crossed collars embroidered with falling rain and rice ears in pale green thread, the knees of the outer robe faded almost white from kneeling at the rites, a pale grey gauze over-robe beaded as though with dew, a plain sash with one small green jade drop; a light rice-straw hat hangs at her back on a silk cord. Hands and objects: the left hand steadies the pole, the right holds a knotted measuring cord; round the right wrist a pale band where a rite bell's cord once rested; a second cut pole leans beside her, its end clearly shorter. Background: black-green bamboo stems rising into drifting mist, a dim path, one far lantern-glow from the hermitage. Light: cold moonlight filtering through the leaves, silver on her hair and a soft green spirit-glow at her hands. Power: a Trúc Cơ cultivator of Wood and Water, so fine green motes and a few drops of rain-mist float around the pole, thin and faint. Expression: grim and watchful, lips tight, the face of someone certain of a wrong and unwilling to name a friend yet. A faint blue-green and silver tint.

people.imagined: A cellar under a lantern-lit grating. He sits on a wooden crate and coils a loose length of cord over his hand without noticing, while a lantern outside lays bars of light across his face; he is waiting for the new moon's question.
people.subject: The moment: a captive sitting on a crate in a cellar, coiling a loose cord round his hand again and again, listening to footsteps above a grating. Face: a lean, weathered, patient face with a long jaw, a few days of grey stubble, steady brown eyes sunk with sleeplessness, a straight nose, a faint scar through one brow; a loyal, closed mouth. Hair: black and grey, long, loosened from its knot and tucked behind his ears, the jade pine-twig pin missing. Body: wiry and rope-strong, forearms corded, sitting upright with his back to the wall, ankles close together. Clothing: the pine-green and pale bark-cream robes of Tùng Đào Cung, creased and faded from many days in the damp, the hem grey with cellar dust, the collars still showing their pine needles and wind-curls in darker green thread; no sash and no pendant, they were taken, so the outer robe hangs open over the cream inner layer; the sleeves are pushed to the elbow. Hands and objects: rope-burn lines run across both palms, the right hand turning a thin hemp cord into neat coils; beside him a wooden cup of water and an empty bowl. Background: a low brick cellar with a damp wall, hanging roots, a barred grating high above with leaves pressed against it, deep shadow in the corners. Light: pale moonlight and amber lantern-glow falling through the grating in bars across his chest and face, with a faint cold mist rising from the floor. Expression: calm, patient and unbroken, eyes lifted toward the grating; he is thinking about a rope on a bridge and says nothing. A faint green-grey tint.

people.imagined: On Thương Ưng Đài at dusk, wind rising. The head of Phất Y Cốc stands side-on to the viewer at the terrace edge, the founder's grey sleeve streaming, as though about to leave, one hand resting on a plain sword.
people.subject: The moment: dusk on a high windy terrace, a tall man standing side-on to the viewer at the edge, face turned toward the open distance as though he were about to leave. Face: a long, quiet, weathered face, high cheekbones, a strong straight nose, a thin humble mouth, grey-brown eyes narrowed against the wind, a few fine lines at the corners; shaven except for a short grey-streaked moustache. Hair: black threaded with silver, bound in a high knot under a plain silver crown, loose strands streaming sideways. Body: tall, spare and upright, the narrow shoulders of a sword cultivator who gives nothing away, feet planted lightly. Clothing: long robes of the finest grey silk in three layers, a silver-grey gauze over-robe lifting in the wind, collars edged in charcoal, the left sleeve very long and flowing far past his hand like a banner, borders of a faint silver wind-curl pattern; a narrow sash with a small silver sword-token; the grey of the whole outfit is old and soft, the head's richest cut worn without show. Hands and objects: the right hand rests on the hilt of a plain sword in a dark scabbard at his hip, thumb on the guard; the left is hidden in the long sleeve. Background: a stone terrace, a far plateau sinking into violet haze, two hawks turning on the wind below. Light: gold-pink dusk light from the right and a cold silver rim along his profile and sleeve. Power: a Kết Đan cultivator of Metal with a Wind gift, so silver-white glints and thin pale streams of wind curl along the sword and the long sleeve, bright but restrained. Expression: humble, withdrawn and calm, the look of someone listening to a duel he will not describe. A faint silver-grey tint.

people.imagined: Dusk in Đà Linh Trấn. A rider for hire sits on a mounting block with his sabre across his knees, grinning a moment too long at someone just out of the picture; the rust-brown front teeth show.
people.subject: The moment: dusk in a desert-edge town, a lone hired rider sitting on a stone mounting block with a sabre across his knees, grinning a moment too long at someone just out of frame. Face: a lean, sun-cracked face of sand-brown skin, a hawk nose, a thin dark moustache, pale restless eyes under heavy lids, front teeth stained a rust brown that no scrubbing shifts, shown in a slow wide grin; a voice that looks worn soft as sand. Hair: dark brown, oiled back and gathered in a short tail with a copper ring. Body: lean, long-limbed, slouched at ease but with the readiness of a wolf; one ankle across his knee. Clothing: layered silk robes in sand-gold and rust red, the crossed collars edged in smoky black with a thin ember-orange line, a wide black gauze over-robe split at the sides for riding, bracers of dark lacquered scale at the wrists, a belt of linked bronze plates; graceful, a little cruel, a robe cut for a rider who took his teaching with him from a sect that threw him out. Hands and objects: both hands rest on a curved sabre in a red-lacquered scabbard, the blade half drawn, a red tassel dangling; the right thumb runs over the bright edge. Background: an adobe town street with hanging lamps, a tethered horse, long violet shadows, a thin dust haze. Light: low amber dusk from the left and warm ember-glow rising from the sabre onto his chin. Power: a Trúc Cơ cultivator whose roots are Fire, Earth and Metal, so a shimmer of dull red heat and a few sand-coloured motes rise around the blade. Expression: a lazy, pleased, unreadable grin, calm and cold in the eyes. Palette: sand, rust, ember orange, black.

people.imagined: Remembered: at sixty in the Đới house at Tang Điền, drawing one unbroken thread from a basin of cocoons, singing the old reeling songs low, steam rising round her face.
people.subject: The moment: a memorial portrait of a reeler at the reeling basin of a silk house, at sixty, drawing a single unbroken thread up from a bowl of cocoons while she sings the old reeling songs under her breath. Face: a round, patient, deeply lined face with soft cheeks, small calm dark eyes lowered on the thread, a gently curved mouth, faint damp-flushed colour on the cheeks; the face of a woman who has breathed steam all her life. Hair: grey, drawn back into a neat coil under a cocoon-white headcloth tied at the nape. Body: sturdy and a little stooped, small strong shoulders, sitting very straight at the basin. Clothing: a house robe of fine undyed cocoon-white silk in two layers, the crossed collar and wide sleeves bordered in a narrow line of fire-red thread worked in tiny thread-loops, sleeves tied back with silk cords, a pale gauze over-robe, a plain pearl-coloured sash; the richness of a Foundation cultivator who never went back to her mountain, simple and clean. Hands and objects: both hands lift a glistening single thread of silk, fine as a hair, from a copper basin of warm water with pale cocoons turning in it; a wooden reeling frame and a small spool beside her. Background: a warm silk house with hanging skeins of pale thread, wooden racks, rising steam, a window of soft light. Light: soft spirit-light from the upper left, a pale gold glow gathering along the thread as though it were lit from within, a gentle rim light on her hair. Expression: a quiet, absorbed half-smile, the face of a woman keeping a song unbroken for those who come after. The whole picture faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened, with a faint warm cream and pale-red tint.
